step_by_step_reasoning: We start by mapping the user actors to UserConsumerWeb to represent the independent insurance agents. The static web application is hosted in an S3 bucket and cached/distributed globally via CloudFront, which we model as Flow 0. API traffic is routed through CloudFront to API Gateway (Flow 1). We model two distinct Lambda nodes because they serve separate logical architectural roles: one is the custom Authorizer Lambda for validating user access, and the other is the Python Business Logic Lambda executing backend workloads. This Python Lambda interfaces with DynamoDB to manage and cache regional user session states across multiple Availability Zones, and integrates bi-directionally with legacy Java Tomcat application servers running on EC2 to support unmigrated functionalities.

edges.notes: User requests single-page application web assets.
CloudFront retrieves static SPA assets from S3.
User sends dynamic API traffic to CloudFront.
CloudFront routes backend API calls to API Gateway.
API Gateway triggers Lambda authorizer to authenticate user.
API Gateway forwards authorized dynamic requests to the python microservice Lambda.
Lambda reads and writes cached user session info.
Python Lambda delegates unmigrated calls to legacy Tomcat application.
Legacy Tomcat application returns payload back to modern serverless backend.
